answer: Spatial challenge-response attestation. Each agent identity must answer a fresh, signed timing challenge sent to a fixed hardware beacon it claims to house, requiring a round-trip under a strict microsecond bound. Beacons sit in shielded enclosures at disclosed coordinates, so an oasis deployment and a karst ridge site yield distinguishable propagation delays. An attacker cannot fake co-location: relaying through a network adds delay exceeding the bound at the zenith of tolerance.
